decision_reason: A1 leaves waist bends forward close to knees bending (crouching), represents climbing stairs and jump front & back with weakly resolved whole-body posture and translation concepts, and gives jump front & back the weakest seen-class coverage. Splitting global posture variability into trunk and lower-limb components creates a transferable distinction for trunk flexion versus leg-driven motion. Vertical whole-body excursion and translation-direction consistency further distinguish climbing stairs from level locomotion and separate consistently progressing climbing stairs from direction-reversing jump front & back. Motion regularity is dropped because every supplied A1 prototype has the same High level on that dimension.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: trunk_inclination_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the trunk changes its gravity-relative inclination within a window, independently of orientation changes confined mainly to the limbs.

attributes.name: lower_limb_configuration_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the load-bearing lower-limb configuration changes within a window, as indicated by gravity-relative ankle-region orientation and its relation to trunk motion.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: vertical_body_excursion
attributes.definition: Prominence of whole-body displacement along the gravity direction, including repeated rising and lowering even when there is little net vertical progression.

levels.Low: Little or no whole-body vertical displacement.
levels.Medium: Moderate vertical displacement or intermittent rising and lowering.
levels.High: Large or repeatedly prominent whole-body vertical displacement.

attributes.name: translation_direction_consistency
attributes.definition: Degree to which whole-body translational motion maintains a consistent progression direction rather than repeatedly stopping or reversing direction.

levels.Low: Little directional progression or frequent translation reversals.
levels.Medium: Partly consistent progression with some stopping or reversal.
levels.High: Sustained translation with a strongly consistent progression direction.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains an independent distinction between static activities and vigorous activities, with running and jogging providing seen support for the high-intensity semantics relevant to climbing stairs and jump front & back.

Repetition rate is physically distinct from motion magnitude and separates faster cyclic movement from static, slow, or moderately repeated movement; walking, cycling, jogging, and running provide transferable cadence anchors.

Sustained rapid fluctuation remains distinct from isolated impacts and helps contrast smooth waist flexion with fluctuation-rich jumping, using frontal elevation of arms, knees bending (crouching), and running as seen anchors.

Short-duration impacts provide a direct transferable distinction between jump front & back and smoother bending activities, with running anchoring strong impact semantics and frontal elevation of arms and knees bending (crouching) anchoring low impact.

Mean gravity-relative global posture remains necessary for standing still and for distinguishing upright locomotion from inclined or horizontal configurations, with sitting and relaxing and lying down supplying ordered static-posture anchors.

The global A1 concept conflates chest-dominant trunk flexion with leg-driven configuration change. Gravity-relative chest and ankle observations can distinguish waist bends forward from its nearest seen anchor knees bending (crouching), while lower-limb variability also transfers to climbing and jumping.

Angular-motion prominence remains physically independent of translation and impact, and transfers from frontal elevation of arms and knees bending (crouching) to the prominent flexion rotation of waist bends forward.

Generic sustained locomotor progression remains useful for separating climbing stairs from in-place bending and static posture, with walking, cycling, jogging, and running providing seen locomotion anchors.
The supplied A1 matrix assigns High motion regularity to every seen and unseen class, so the attribute provides no split-specific contrast despite being physically measurable.

Gravity-referenced whole-body rising and lowering is not isolated by generic translation or posture variability. It connects climbing stairs and jump front & back to the seen leg-driven anchor knees bending (crouching) while distinguishing them from predominantly level locomotion and arm-only movement.

The low-U_NN pair climbing stairs and jump front & back differs in directional organization: stair climbing maintains locomotor progression, whereas front-and-back jumping repeatedly reverses it. Walking, cycling, jogging, and running provide seen examples of consistent progression.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final concepts are physically distinct. Motion intensity measures aggregate energy; cadence measures repetition rate; smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation; impulsiveness measures isolated abrupt peaks. Posture inclination represents mean global configuration, while trunk inclination variability and lower-limb configuration variability represent changes in different body regions. Rotational motion is angular, whereas translational motion is sustained linear progression. Vertical body excursion captures gravity-axis rising and lowering even without net progression, and translation direction consistency captures persistence versus reversal of progression. These two refinements therefore do not duplicate generic translational magnitude. The non-discriminative A1 motion_regularity dimension is removed.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
